entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been made accused for the offences under section 420 IPC, under sections 66(C), 66 (D) of I.T. Act and under sections 17 and 27 of NDPS Act.
He has further stated that no incriminating article has been recovered from the possession of the petitioner.

The learned counsel has further stated that three of the co-accused persons, namely, Sunil Kumar, Md. Saddam and Md. Jasim have been granted bail by a coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 17.5.2024 passed in BA Nos. 4068 of 2024, 4086 of 2024 and 4120 of 2024 and the case of the petitioner stands on similar footing.

Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for bail but has not denied the cited bail orders.
Having heard learned counsels for the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to release the above named petitioner on bail, on executing bail-bond of Rs. 25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, NDPS cases, Chatra, in connection with Simariya PS Case No. 30 of 2024, subject to the conditions that (i) the petitioner shall attend each and every date of trial unless it is dispensed with by the learned court below (ii) the petitioner shall submit Ankit Kumar @ Golu Saw vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ...
